subject.title: fix(codex): continue after source-reply delivery instead of terminating turn

question: Should this message-delivery change require a live Codex-backed channel run proving intermediate delivery, subsequent tool execution, one final reply, and no duplicate recovery before merge?
rationale: Focused tests support the classifier change, but only maintainers can accept or waive the real-channel exactly-once proof for this delivery-sensitive behavior, especially while current main and a competing PR have diverged.

options.title: Require live exactly-once proof
options.body: Keep one rebased candidate open until a redacted Discord/Codex transcript or runtime log proves continuation and non-duplication through the real delivery path.

options.title: Accept focused runtime tests
options.body: Treat the bridge tests and CI as sufficient despite the unresolved real-channel delivery and recovery uncertainty.

options.title: Retire both branches
options.body: If current-main history confirms the refactored bridge already owns the behavior, close both candidate PRs and the linked issue with the canonical fix commit.

recommendation.title: Require live exactly-once proof
recommendation.body: Keep one rebased candidate open until a redacted Discord/Codex transcript or runtime log proves continuation and non-duplication through the real delivery path.

likelyOwner.reason: The generic continuation and duplicate-suppression contract originates in this person's merged work, making them the strongest available owner for the proof boundary.
